title: Basic SIR Model
text: use data simulated basic SIR model 500 households. assume individuals start susceptible. per day intra-household infection probability 5% daily extra-household infection probability 1%.

title: Basic SIR Model
text: addition data, user needs specify underlying model structure, involves two components: infection process model specifies underlying compartmental model structure. observation process model specifies probability observing positive outcome given individual compartment infection process model.

title: Basic SIR Model
text: infection process model built series user-defined transitions. two types transitions: transmit() defines transition occurs result infection (e.g. S>) progress() defines non-infection transition occurs constant rate (e.g. ->R). functions, user specifies destination (e.g = S) source (e.g = ) compartment. Additionally progress() transitions, user must enter parameter transition rate. name parameter discretion user (e.g. gamma recovery rate) can set specific numeric value NA model fit parameter.
code: # Basic SIR, fit recovery rate inf_process <- make_infection_model(transmit(from = "S", to = "I"),                                     progress(from = "I", to = "R", gamma = NA))

title: Basic SIR Model
text: observation model composed series named vectors. vector corresponds observation type. entry vector named corresponding compartment infection process model. value probability observing positive observation given individual compartment. example two observation types, one likely positive person actively infectious (e.g. PCR test results) likely positive person recovered immune infection (e.g. IgG antibody). Now ready run model! Now let’s look model results using posterior package.
code: obs_process <- make_observation_model(   pcr = c("S" = 0.05, "I" = 0.95, "R" = 0.05),   igg = c("S" = 0.01, "I" = 0.01, "R" = 0.8) ) # Note this is very computationally intensive so the block is not evaluated # when knitting  ## Inputs # 1. Infection process model # 2. Observation process model # 3. Raw data # 4. Covariates (optional) # 5. Starting state probabilities  sir_res <- run_model(   inf_model = inf_process,   obs_model = obs_process,   data = sir,   init_probs = c(1 - 2 * 1e-10, 1e-10, 1e-10),   stan_opts = stan_options(iter = 1000) ) # The output from the model in the previous code chunk is available in the # sir_res package data object  # Get summary statistics. Parameters are returned on the natural (model) scale, # so no back-transformation is needed. draws_sum <- summarise_draws(sir_res, "mean", "median", ~ quantile2(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))) |>   mutate(var_type = c(rep("Infection probability", 2), "Recovery rate"))  # "True" values from underlying simulation draws_sum$true_value <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.2)  draws_sum ## # A tibble: 3 × 7 ##   variable    mean  median    q2.5  q97.5 var_type              true_value ##   <chr>      <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>                      <dbl> ## 1 eh_prob  0.00984 0.00984 0.00911 0.0105 Infection probability       0.01 ## 2 ih_prob  0.0545  0.0545  0.0486  0.0607 Infection probability       0.05 ## 3 gamma    0.203   0.203   0.192   0.213  Recovery rate               0.2

title: Basic SIR Model
text: can add covariates intra- extra-household infection risk including optional ih_cov eh_cov arguments, respectively, run_model(). Let’s take look results .
code: # Simulated data from a basic SIR model for 500 households head(sir_cov$observations)  # Run model with x1 and x2 as covariates sir_cov_res <- run_model(   inf_model = inf_process,   obs_model = obs_process,   data = sir_cov$observations,   ih_cov = sir_cov$covariates,   eh_cov = sir_cov$covariates,   init_probs = c(1 - 2 * 1e-10, 1e-10, 1e-10),   stan_opts = stan_options(iter = 1000) ) # The output from the model in the previous code chunk is available in the # sir_cov_res package data object  # Get summary statistics. Infection probabilities and rates are returned on the # natural (model) scale and coefficients on the natural (exponentiated) scale, # so no back-transformation is needed. draws_sum <- summarise_draws(sir_cov_res, "mean", "median",                              ~ quantile2(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))) |>   mutate(var_type = c(rep("Infection probability", 2), "Recovery rate", rep("Coefficient", 4)))  # "True" values from underlying simulation draws_sum$true_vals <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.2, exp(-0.4), exp(0.7), exp(0.8), exp(0.1))  draws_sum ## # A tibble: 7 × 7 ##   variable    mean  median    q2.5  q97.5 var_type              true_vals ##   <chr>      <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>                     <dbl> ## 1 eh_prob  0.00961 0.00960 0.00853 0.0108 Infection probability     0.01  ## 2 ih_prob  0.0509  0.0509  0.0425  0.0594 Infection probability     0.05  ## 3 gamma    0.197   0.197   0.187   0.208  Recovery rate             0.2   ## 4 x1_eh    0.636   0.634   0.538   0.746  Coefficient               0.670 ## 5 x2_eh    2.03    2.03    1.75    2.37   Coefficient               2.01  ## 6 x1_ih    2.22    2.20    1.77    2.74   Coefficient               2.23  ## 7 x2_ih    0.857   0.851   0.659   1.10   Coefficient               1.11

title: Parallel and threaded fitting (including HPC)
text: Threading unless ask , ask stan_options() already pass run_model(): stan_opts works laptop inside scheduled job: flexstanr sizes fit allocation process actually , machine’s total core count. See flexstanr article allocation rules job-script templates, substituting run_model() fit call shown .
code: # detect the cores this process is allowed to use and split them automatically fit <- run_model(   inf_model  = inf_process,   obs_model  = obs_process,   data       = sir,   init_probs = c(1 - 2 * 1e-10, 1e-10, 1e-10),   stan_opts  = stan_options(chains = 4, iter = 1000, threading = TRUE) )  # cap the pool, for example to keep some cores free fit <- run_model(   ...,   stan_opts = stan_options(chains = 4, threading = TRUE, max_cores = 6) )  # single-threaded (the default): manage backend parallelism yourself fit <- run_model(..., stan_opts = stan_options(threading = FALSE))

title: Bayesian Compartmental Infection Models from Individual Outcomes
text: {hestia} fits Bayesian compartmental infection models — susceptible-infected-recovered (SIR) multi-compartment hidden Markov variants — individual-level outcome data. Models composed infection-process observation-process components fit using Stan via rstan.

title: Bayesian Compartmental Infection Models from Individual Outcomes
text: Requires R >= 4.1.0 C++ toolchain (Stan model compilation).

title: Bayesian Compartmental Infection Models from Individual Outcomes
text: Compose infection-process model transmit() (transmission compartments) progress() (within-host progression) steps: Pair infection process observation model (make_observation_model()) fit run_model(). See vignettes full worked examples, including multi-compartment (symptomatic/asymptomatic) model.
code: library(hestia)  # A basic SIR model: S -> I transmission, I -> R recovery (rate fit from data) inf_process <- make_infection_model(   transmit(from = "S", to = "I"),   progress(from = "I", to = "R", gamma = NA) )

title: Create Transmission Probability Matrix — get_transmission_details
text: list following entries: "states", character vector state names "trans_matrix", matrix transition rate values origin (column) destination (row) compartments given. values provided transition rates entry equal 1e-10. "mult_matrix", matrix split values transition origin (column) destination (row) compartments given. split values provided transition rates entry equal 1. "trans_to_fit", data frame information transitions within model, parameter indexing details transition rate fit "mult_to_fit", data frame information splits specified model, parameter indexing details split fit "inf_states", numeric values corresponding indices "states" infectious states "mult_ih_inf_probs", indicator whether infectious states shared separate inta-household infection probabilities. FALSE infection probabilities shared across infectious compartments.

title: Create Transmission Probability Matrix — get_transmission_details
code: # Split the infectious compartment into symptomatic (I_s) and asymptomatic # (I_a) infections, with separate intra-household infection probabilities. inf_model <- make_infection_model(   transmit(from = "S",            to = c("I_s", "I_a"),            source = c("I_s", "I_a"),            split = "phi"),   progress(from = "I_s", to = "R", gamma_s = NA),   progress(from = "I_a", to = "R", gamma_a = NA),   mult_ih_inf_probs = TRUE)  get_transmission_details(inf_model) #> $states #> [1] "S"   "I_s" "I_a" "R"   #>  #> $trans_matrix #>        from_S from_I_s from_I_a from_R #> to_S    1e-10    1e-10    1e-10  1e-10 #> to_I_s  1e-10    1e-10    1e-10  1e-10 #> to_I_a  1e-10    1e-10    1e-10  1e-10 #> to_R    1e-10    1e-10    1e-10  1e-10 #>  #> $mult_matrix #>        from_S from_I_s from_I_a from_R #> to_S        1        1        1      1 #> to_I_s      1        1        1      1 #> to_I_a      1        1        1      1 #> to_R        1        1        1      1 #>  #> $trans_to_fit #>   from  to trans_row trans_col rate_name param source #> 1    S I_s         2         1      <NA>     0   2, 3 #> 2    S I_a         3         1      <NA>     0   2, 3 #> 3  I_s   R         4         2   gamma_s     1      0 #> 4  I_a   R         4         3   gamma_a     2      0 #>  #> $mult_to_fit #>   from  to mult_row mult_col mult_name param #> 1    S I_s        2        1       phi     1 #> 2    S I_a        3        1     1-phi    -1 #>  #> $inf_states #> [1] 2 3 #>  #> $mult_ih_inf_probs #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $mult_eh_inf_probs #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $compete #> [1] 0 0 0 0 #>

title: hestia 0.1.0
text: Stan fitting draw extraction now use flexstanr. Configure automatic, scheduler-aware within-chain threading stan_options(threading = TRUE). First release. Fit Bayesian compartmental infection models individual-level outcome data, using Stan via ‘rstan’. Models composed infection process observation process fit single call. Infection-process building blocks: transmit() progress() define transitions, assembled make_infection_model(). Susceptible-infected- recovered (SIR), split symptomatic/asymptomatic (SIIR), similar multi-compartment structures supported. make_observation_model() defines observation process (per-compartment detection probabilities one tests). run_model() fits assembled model data returns posterior draws natural (model) scale. get_transmission_details() exposes parameter structure infection model. Bundled simulated datasets fitted-draw fixtures examples vignettes: sir, sir_cov, siir, sir_res, sir_cov_res, siir_res posterior draws. Vignettes: “SIR” “multiple infection compartments”.
